name: Sprite boards
readme: Sprite reference boards: the hero sheet (approved) and the animation, enemy, item and boss boards that follow the [visual direction](../direction/README.md). Each board is drawn from real photos of the pose or object, keyed on magenta and crushed to a transparent 1x image. Frame lists and status are in [07 – Asset manifest](../../docs/07-ASSET-MANIFEST.md); the pipeline is in [09](../../docs/09-ART-PIPELINE.md). The [poncho photo board](source-boards/ponchos.png) is the source for the hero's poncho.
style: Detailed modern HI-BIT PIXEL ART in the look of a modern detailed pixel-art side-scroller: crisp square pixels at a fine 2-pixel grain, rich naturalistic palette with warm autumn light, careful pixel shading and texture (rust, fabric weave, plastic sheen), no anti-aliasing blur, no smooth vector gradients, not chunky 8-bit, not chibi. This is a SPRITE SHEET, not an illustration: no landscape, no sky, no scenery, no panels, no UI frames. Rules: strict side view unless the brief says otherwise; every sprite on the same invisible ground line, same scale within the sheet, evenly spaced with clear empty space between sprites so each can be cut out; frames progress by small continuous changes so they animate smoothly. Solid flat pure magenta #FF00FF background everywhere, no floor, no cast shadows on the background, no frame borders. ABSOLUTELY NO TEXT: no titles, no frame numbers, no arrows, no captions, no labels, no logos - only sprites on magenta. Match the pixel grain, palette and warm rim light of the game's style master (the LAST image), but draw nothing of its scenery. WORLD SCALE: the hero is an adult 6 ft (183 cm) tall; Dexter (the Deggster panther plush) is 1.5 ft (45 cm); Dexter's final form is 8.5 ft (260 cm). Keep real-world proportions between characters and props (a chair seat is at the hero's knee height, a cafeteria tray is as wide as the hero's shoulders).
people: The photos show real people only to demonstrate a pose. Never draw those people: draw OUR hero from the hero sheet (first image) instead - 6 ft adult in the grey/blue/teal THD poncho with tassels, deep hood that shows only black shadow (face, hair and gender are NEVER visible), black backpack, grey jeans, white sneakers - copying only the body pose, grip, weight shift and the prop's angle.

boards.title: The student · hero design
boards.prompt: Keep the body, height (6 ft adult), proportions, pose, backpack, grey slim jeans and chunky white sneakers of the hero in the first image, and the poncho's CUT, tassel fringe and geometric zig-zag weave from the second image, but RECOLOUR and redesign the poncho as the university's own THD poncho: heather-grey base, deep THD blue and teal zig-zag bands, with a few thin colourful accent stripes (orange, cream, a little red). The poncho has its OWN deep hood, always up. The face is NEVER visible: inside the hood is only solid dark shadow - no eyes, no glasses, no hair, no chin. Gender must be impossible to tell: no visible hair, no visible face, loose silhouette. No hoodie, no scarf. Clean pixel-art CHARACTER SHEET on a flat magenta background, no scenery and no panels. Row 1, full-body turnaround, 5 figures at identical scale: front, three-quarter front, side facing right, three-quarter back, BACK - on the back the poncho has a bold woven THD crest patch in cream and blue with the letters THD clearly readable. Row 2: a close-up of the hood (pure shadow inside), a close-up of the THD back patch, then a scale lineup on one ground line: the hero, a 1.5 ft black panther plush mascot in a grey T-shirt at knee height (third image), and an 8.5 ft tall shadowy panther-humanoid silhouette with glowing blue eyes.
boards.note: Approved 23 Oct 2026. Drawn from earlier iterations (design anchor outside Git); never redrawn - every other board uses its committed preview.
boards.review: ✅ Approved 23 Oct. Adult 6 ft, face never visible, THD poncho in grey / THD blue / teal with colourful accents, THD crest on the back, scale lineup with Dexter (1.5 ft) and his final form (8.5 ft). Fourth iteration: chibi proportions, a hoodie and a visible face were rejected along the way.

boards.title: The student · walk
boards.prompt: On a flat, solid, pure magenta #FF00FF background (no paper colour, no ground shadows, no dust under the feet), with NO text at all - no titles, no captions, no frame numbers, no labels under the figures: Hero from the first image (keep the THD poncho, the shadow-filled hood and all proportions exactly), facing right, strict side view, identical scale in every frame. 2 rows. Row 1, exactly 8 figures: IDLE breathing loop, 6 frames (relaxed stance, the poncho rises and settles, tassels sway a little), then IDLE TO WALK, 2 frames (weight shifts forward, the front foot lifts). Row 2, exactly 8 figures: WALK cycle in key poses with clearly different leg positions - contact (legs wide apart, heel down), down, passing (legs together), up, for the right leg, then the same four for the left leg; the poncho hem swings against the legs, the backpack bobs. The THD crest patch is on the poncho's BACK only and is never visible from the side. Every figure stands on the SAME invisible ground line, even airborne poses: the game moves the body, so never draw a figure higher up. Each row's figures are evenly spaced from left to right with wide clear magenta gaps between neighbours: no tassel, foot, hand or poncho edge touches the next figure, and rows are separated by empty magenta bands. Draw distinct key poses, never blurred in-betweens; neighbouring frames change by small continuous steps so they loop smoothly. Count the figures: each row has EXACTLY the number stated.
boards.review: 🟡 Drawn 23 Oct, waiting for Alexander's Design review. Counts match docs/07 and the atlas slices cleanly; the looping previews below are at twice game size.

boards.title: Campus robot · collectible companion
boards.prompt: Companion sprite sheet: the cute boxy campus delivery robot from the photos (the images after the first) (dark grey sheet-metal box body, two round sensor eyes on the front, small black lidar puck on top, four chunky black rubber wheels, a yellow-black hazard strip, THD lettering on the side). It is knee-high to the 6 ft hero from the first image; draw the hero once at the start of row 1 for scale. Row 1: idle - eyes blink, lidar spins, 4 frames. Row 2: following the player, drive cycle 6 frames. Row 3: happy hop 3 frames, scanning beam from its eyes 3 frames, sleeping (eyes dark, slumped) 2 frames.

boards.title: The student · hurt, death, interact
boards.prompt: Hero from the first image (keep the THD poncho, the shadow-filled hood and all proportions exactly), facing right, side view, identical scale in every frame. Row 1: take damage - white hit-flash silhouette, recoil backwards, stagger, recover: 4 frames; then knockback launched backwards through the air, 3 frames. Row 2: death - collapse to knees, fall forward, lying still with the poncho spread out, fade into pixel dust: 6 frames. Row 3: interact - reach out and touch something at chest height, 3 frames; crouch and pick up an item from the ground, 4 frames; hold up a small glowing handheld device and look at its screen, 3 frames.

boards.prompt: On a flat, solid, pure magenta #FF00FF background (no paper colour, no ground shadows, no dust under the feet), with NO text at all - no titles, no captions, no frame numbers, no labels under the figures: Hero from the first image (keep the THD poncho, the shadow-filled hood and all proportions exactly), facing right, strict side view, identical scale in every frame. 3 rows. Row 1, exactly 9 figures: JUMP - crouch anticipation, take-off, rise, rise higher, apex (the poncho billows up, tassels float), turn over, descend, landing squash, recover to standing. Row 2, exactly 7 figures: FALL loop, 3 frames (poncho flapping upward, arms out for balance), then HARD LANDING, 4 frames (deep impact crouch with one hand on the ground and a puff of dust, push up, straighten, stand). Row 3, exactly 4 figures: CLIMBING A LADDER seen from BEHIND (back to the viewer, the THD crest patch on the poncho's back visible, hood up), hands and feet alternating on invisible rungs in a 4-frame loop; do not draw the ladder itself. Every figure stands on the SAME invisible ground line, even airborne poses: the game moves the body, so never draw a figure higher up. boards.title: Chair · side sweep
boards.prompt: Weapon: the honey-coloured bent-plywood stacking chair with four thin black steel legs from the photos (the images after the first). Animation for a HORIZONTAL SIDE ATTACK with the chair, hero facing right, 8 frames in one row, then the same 8 frames repeated in row 2 as a clean silhouette-only version in dark grey (for timing review). Frames: 1 ready stance holding the chair by the seat at hip height, legs pointing back; 2 anticipation, body twists back, chair pulled behind; 3 start of swing; 4 fast swing smear (chair blurred into a pixel smear arc, legs forward); 5 contact frame, chair fully extended in front at waist height with a small white impact spark; 6 follow-through past the body; 7 recovery, weight back on the rear foot; 8 back to ready. Copy the grips and the low wide stance from the photos (the images after the first). Row 3: the chair alone at the same pixel scale in 4 orientations (upright side view, upside-down, held horizontally, legs-forward).

boards.title: Chair · overhead slam
boards.prompt: Weapon: the bent-plywood chair with thin black steel legs from the photos (the images after the first). Two attack animations, hero facing right. Row 1, UP ATTACK (hits enemies above), 6 frames: crouch with chair low, lift, chair thrust straight overhead seat-up legs to the sky (as in the photos), hold at peak with a small impact spark above, start lowering, back to ready. Row 2, DOWN SLAM (overhead to ground), 7 frames: chair raised high behind the head, peak, fast downward smear arc, chair slammed upright onto the ground in front with a dust burst and small pixel debris, a 1-frame screen-shake pose, hero pulls the chair back up, ready. Row 3, air version of the down slam: hero in the air pointing the chair legs downward (pogo, like a downward strike in Hollow Knight), 4 frames. Copy the weight shift and grips from the photos (the images after the first).

boards.title: Chair · block
boards.prompt: Weapon: the bent-plywood chair with thin black steel legs. BLOCK / GUARD animation, hero facing right, holding the chair seat in front of the chest like a shield with the four legs pointing forward at the enemy, exactly as in the photos. Row 1: raise guard, 4 frames (from ready to full guard). Row 2: hold guard loop, 3 frames (tiny breathing shift); then block-impact reaction, 4 frames: a hit spark on the seat, the hero skids back a few pixels, the chair wobbles, recover. Row 3: guard break, 4 frames: the chair is knocked up and away, hero stumbles back with arms out, then catches the chair again. Keep the sturdy wide stance from the photos (the images after the first).

boards.title: Tray · throw and return
boards.prompt: Ranged weapon: the yellow-beige Mensa cafeteria tray from the photos (the images after the first) (rectangular, rounded corners, raised rim, scuffed matte plastic, faint scratches). Hero facing right. Row 1, THROW, 6 frames: hold the tray flat at the chest with both hands (as in the photos), wind back across the body like a frisbee, release with arm extended, follow-through, empty-handed ready. Row 2: the tray in flight, 8 frames of a spinning cycle seen from the side (flat edge-on, tilted, face-on, tilted, edge-on...) so it reads as a boomerang spinning horizontally, with a short motion trail. Row 3, CATCH, 4 frames: the tray returns, hero catches it, small skid, back to ready. Row 4: the tray alone at the same pixel scale - stack of trays (pickup), single tray face-on, edge-on, and a bent/cracked tray (broken).

boards.title: Enemy · drone
boards.prompt: Enemy sprite sheet: the big black carbon-fibre quadcopter from the photos (four long arms, red-and-black motors, two-bladed props, tall black landing legs, exposed wiring and a small electronics deck in the middle). Make it hostile and slightly uncanny: one red sensor eye on the deck. Side view, about twice as wide as the hero would be tall. Row 1: hover loop, 4 frames (props as blur discs, body bobs 1-2 pixels). Row 2: alert (eye flashes), tilt forward, dive-attack 3 frames with a speed trail, pull up. Row 3: hit flash (white silhouette), knocked sideways and spinning, crashing down, wreck on the ground with one prop still twitching and a little smoke: 5 frames. Row 4: a small projectile it drops (a loose screw / sparking battery), 3 frames.

boards.title: Enemy · rover
boards.prompt: Enemy sprite sheet: the small four-wheeled lab rover from the photos (aluminium chassis, four chunky yellow wheels with black tyres, plywood top deck, black cylindrical lidar on top, two round ultrasonic sensor 'eyes' at the front). Side view facing left, knee-high to the hero. Row 1: idle - lidar spins, 4 frames. Row 2: patrol drive, 6 frames (wheels turn, chassis bounces 1 pixel). Row 3: spot the player - lidar flashes red, rear up a little, then CHARGE ram 4 frames with dust kicked from the wheels. Row 4: hit flash, flipped on its back with wheels spinning, smoking wreck: 5 frames.

boards.title: Enemy · walker
boards.prompt: Enemy sprite sheet: the six-legged hexapod robot from the photos (black and grey servo motors, orange-copper wiring nest on top, long curved black legs ending in points). Make it creep like a spider. Side view facing left, about as tall as the hero's waist, wider than tall. Row 1: idle - legs twitch, 4 frames. Row 2: walk cycle, 8 frames (alternating tripod gait, body level). Row 3: attack - rear up on the back legs with front legs raised, then stab the front legs down, recover: 5 frames. Row 4: hit flash, legs buckle, collapse into a tangled heap with sparks: 5 frames.

boards.title: Boss · Jenny, the runaway race car
boards.prompt: Boss sprite sheet: JENNY, the green-and-black open-wheel Formula Student race car from the team banner photos, now driving itself and haunted: glowing headlight eyes, a slightly crooked front wing, exposed suspension springs. Strict side view, about four times as long as the hero is tall. Row 1: idle - engine revving, body shakes, exhaust puffs, 4 frames. Row 2: charge - wheels spin in place with smoke, then launch forward with speed lines, 4 frames. Row 3: CRASH into a wall - front crumples, car bounces back, parts burst out (springs, bolts, a loose wheel, a wing fragment), 4 frames. Row 4: stunned and vulnerable - smoking, one wheel wobbling, a hazard light blinking, 3 frames; then rebooting and recharging with green sparks, 2 frames. Row 5: the ejected debris as separate small projectiles at the same scale - spring, bolt, wheel, wing shard, battery - each as a 2-frame tumble.

boards.title: Item · pocket computer
boards.prompt: Key item: the aluminium experiment suitcase from the photos (silver case, black screen in the lid, circuit board, coloured buttons and plug sockets inside), shrunk into a hand-held 'pocket computer' the hero carries. Top row: the item as a pickup sprite - closed case glowing softly, 4-frame floating bob; then opened, screen lighting up, 3 frames. Bottom area: three mock in-game screens as the device would show them, drawn in the same pixel style with a green-on-black CRT look: (1) MAP screen - a rough grid map of connected campus rooms with a blinking player dot and unexplored rooms dark; (2) ARCHIVE screen - a list of collected notes as icons (no readable words); (3) MENU screen - icons for items, map, archive, settings. Screens use icons and blocks only, no readable words.

boards.title: Mensa · food pickups
boards.prompt: Healing pickup sprites, copying each photographed item EXACTLY as it really looks, NOT an idealized product shot: the muffin squashed inside wrinkled, glare-streaked cling film with a creased sticker; the marbled chocolate-vanilla cake slice in crumpled cling film on a white paper; the chocolate-coated wafer in its yellow-red foil wrapper (no readable brand); the Leberkaese roll in a torn brown paper bag with the meat slice sticking out unevenly. Row 1: each item large, slightly lopsided, with the real imperfections and reflections. Row 2: each item as a small in-game pickup (about 16 pixels) with a 2-frame sparkle. Row 3: a 'being eaten' sequence for the Leberkaese roll - whole, one bite, two bites, crumbs - 4 frames.

boards.title: Mensa · drinks and coffee
boards.prompt: Pickup and prop sprites copying the photographed items exactly as they look, with real wear, condensation and reflections, NOT cleaned-up product renders, and with no readable brand names (keep only colour blocks and shapes): the brown-and-white iced coffee cup with a brown lid; the green-red strawberry milk carton with white cap; the bottle of iced tea with green cap and green label; a white cafeteria mug with a blue logo block. Row 1: each item large. Row 2: each as a small in-game pickup (about 16 pixels) with a 2-frame sparkle. Row 3: the black-and-steel self-service coffee machine with its glowing touchscreen and green side light, as an interactable prop (save point), 3 frames: idle, screen flicker, pouring coffee into a mug.

boards.title: Wayfinder sign · prop and pole weapon
boards.prompt: Prop and weapon sprites from the campus sign photos: a grey galvanised steel pole with a green square 'assembly point' pictogram sign on top and a yellow town-entrance-style sign below (black arrows; the lower half crossed out with a red diagonal bar), slightly dirty, bolts and clamps visible, standing in gravel. Row 1: the sign as a world prop in front of two backdrops cut as side strips - the vertical-timber-clad building and the pink-render campus facade - 2 versions, side view, plus the sign glitching (pixels torn sideways) 2 frames. Row 2: the hero  crouches at the base of the pole and pulls it out of the ground like in the last two photos, 5 frames: crouch and grip, strain, pole loosens with gravel spraying, yank free, stand holding the pole. Row 3: the pole used as a long weapon, 5 frames: thrust forward, full extension with the sign as a heavy head, recovery.

boards.title: Dexter · the Deggster plush
boards.prompt: Character sheet for DEXTER: the university's black panther mascot plush from the photos (the images after the first) (black velvety fur, ice-blue cat eyes, orange-brown nose, small white fangs, long white whiskers, light-grey T-shirt with a faint round crest, pale grey trousers, black paws with white claw stitches). He is 1.5 ft tall - about knee height to the 6 ft hero from the first image. Same pixel style as the hero sheet. Row 1: turnaround (front, side facing right, back), and the hero standing beside him for scale. Row 2: animations - idle bob 3 frames; plush hop-walk 4 frames; beckoning 'follow me' wave 3 frames. Row 3: emotions - apologetic bow with paws together, nervous sweat, proud while holding up a small glowing pocket computer, and one creepy frame where his shadow on the ground is enormous with a too-wide grin (he is the secret boss). Row 4: Dexter's FINAL FORM, 8.5 ft tall, much taller than the hero (draw the hero beside it for scale): the same plush panther grown into a towering, lanky humanoid, fur matted, seams split with glowing blue light leaking out, T-shirt torn, claws out; 3 poses: stand, menace, lunge.

boards.title: Intro · the lake anomaly
boards.prompt: Storyboard strip, 8 panels in a 4x2 grid separated by thin black gutters (the magenta rule does NOT apply here: each panel has a full side-view pixel-art scene of the Hidden Garden lake from the reference: reeds, stone edge, water). Panels: 1 the hero follows Dexter, who hops ahead toward the lake; 2 Dexter stops at the water's edge and points at a strange glowing ripple; 3 the hero touches the surface - white hit flash; 4 the hero is knocked back in the classic damage pose; 5 instead of landing, the hero is lifted into the air spinning like a starfish, pixels tearing around them; 6 a frozen frame with a grey old-desktop-style error dialog box drawn over the scene (empty title bar, an X icon, blank text lines, a single OK button - no readable words); 7 cut to black with a few glitch lines; 8 the hero lands in a new, darker overgrown area, finishing the damage animation, Dexter nowhere to be seen.
